column2: In that fault of Samgraha one should not have a marriage performed. With the Moon joined to the Sun, poverty clearly arises;
with Mars, death and disease; with Mercury, childlessness; with Jupiter, misfortune; with Venus, children;
with Saturn, renunciation; with Rahu, destruction of the root; with Ketu, constant trouble and poverty for the Moon.
With the Moon joined with malefics, death of the couple; with the Moon joined with benefics, in its exaltation or friend's sign,
the ascendant is of mixed fault and always for the good of the couple, even with Moon exalted, in its own house or in a friend's.
The Moon joined with malefics causes the death of the two. The eighth ascendant of the couple, and the eighth sign;
if it is in the ascendant, it too gives death to the couple. If that sign is joined with benefics, or the ascendant joined with benefics,
one should carefully avoid the ascendant, its division and its lord. The twelfth ascendant of the couple, or if the sign is in the ascendant,
brings loss of wealth to them; avoid the lord of that division. The birth-sign rising and the birth-ascendant rising are good;

the houses of increase (upachaya) for them give auspiciousness through the ascendant. (Then follows a coded list of numbers for the fixed ghatikas of the "poison-nadis" in each star, by word-numbers: sky-arrows, Veda-fortnights, etc.)
(Continuation of the coded numerals for the poison-nadi in each lunar star.)
(Continuation of the coded numerals.)
(Continuation: in order from Ashvini.)
After those, the four ghatikas are called "poison"; in marriage and other rites one should avoid the poison-nadi.
The muhurtas condemned on Sunday and other days should be avoided in marriage and the like, even if endowed with a hundred-thousand virtues.
The weekday faults laid down in order for Sunday and the rest should be avoided in every auspicious rite, even if endowed with all merits.
An ascendant equal to the single "Argala" foot should be avoided, even if joined with Venus and Jupiter, like milk mixed with poison.
Stars of eclipse and omen are to be avoided in auspicious rites for three seasons; the star left by the Moon is like burnt wood.
In auspicious rites one should avoid a star pierced by the cruel and joined with cruel ones, the entire star, as the five cow-products with a drop of liquor.
A star pierced by benefics in a quarter is not inauspicious as a whole; one pierced by cruel ones or joined with them is not at all auspicious.
The navamsas of Libra, Gemini, Virgo, and the last half of Sagittarius are auspicious; those of Taurus too.
The last navamsas are also auspicious if they are "vargottama". The other navamsas are not to be accepted, since they are bad navamsas.
An ascendant in a bad navamsa should be avoided even with all merits. The day on which there is Mahapata should be avoided in auspicious rites,
even if endowed with all merits, since it gives death to the couple. Lesser faults not mentioned are lightning, mist and rain,
opposite sun-halo, rainbow, thunder of clouds, the Latta, Upagraha, Pata, tithis called month-burnt (masadagdha),
burnt ascendants, and signs called blind, deaf and lame. Such as these — their arrangement is now made.
Lightning, mist and rain at the wrong time are certainly a fault in auspicious rites; at the right time they are not a fault.
Jupiter in a centre, or Venus, or Mercury — even one of them removes a mass of faults, without doubt.
Five cross-lines and five upright lines, and two in each corner: in the second Shambhu corner, he should place the fire-star in the diagram.
Here, the stars with Abhijit, one line-planet pierces the star; before and behind, the Sun and the rest strike the star of the day.
The Sun's form, qualities...: stars counted by "arrow, eight, nine"; from the Sun's star, Ashlesha, Magha, Revati, Chitra, Anuradha, Shravana.
By counting the stars of the day, the star pierced from Ashvini by Pata is bad. In Saurashtra and Salva country one should avoid the Latta-struck star.
In Kalinga and Vanga the fallen (pata) star is not auspicious; in Bahlika and the Kuru country, elsewhere there is no fault.
Tithis called month-burnt and the burnt ascendants should be avoided in Madhyadesha; they are not seen to be so in others.
The sign-groups of blind-division ascendants and the signs void in the month should be avoided in Gauda and Malava, not condemned in other countries.
A time always spoiled by fault cannot be wiped away; one should accept what has few faults and more virtues.
Thus at a good ascendant one should have the couple properly looked on. A platform raised a hand's breadth, four cubits square all round,
with four very smooth pillars, bending toward the left side, with a pavilion in the four directions, adorned with steps;
sloping toward the east and north, with plantain pillars, decorated with swans, parrots and the like, various painted pots and sprouts for arches,
adorned with heaps of flowers for decoration and with colours, charming with divine Brahmin blessings and auspicious prosperity,
pleasing the heart with instruments, dance, song and the like. The couple should mount such a fire-altar.
Rashi-kuta is eightfold: the star-group, the sign, the sign-lord, the womb, the class, the season, and sons and grandsons.
When the couple are in the same sign but different stars, the clasping of hands is best, middle or different, according to oneness of sign.
Marriage in the same star and sign brings loss of life. From the woman's star, in the first nine, the woman is far and much condemned;
in the second nine, middling and best; in the third nine, men's. The three Purva and Uttara, Dhatri (Rohini), Yamya (Bharani) and Maheshvara (Ardra) stars,

This is known as the human group (martya-gana); the other is the divine group (amartya-gana): the stars named Hari, Aditya, Arka, Vayu, Antya, Mitra, Ashvini, Indu and Jiva (the names as given in the text).
The demon group (rakshas-gana): the stars named Pitri, Tvashtra, Dvidaiva, Agni, Indra, joined with those named Vasu, Varuna, Mula and Ahi (as given in the text).
If the couple's birth stars are in one group, there is love in many ways; the middling is between gods and humans; between demons and the other, death.
With sixth-eighth, death; with fifth-ninth, childlessness; with second-twelfth, poverty; in others the couple's love is best.
With one lord or friendly status, the clasping of hands is good; with second-twelfth and trine, never sixth-eighth.
The animal "wombs" of the stars, as listed in the text: horse, elephant, ram, serpent, and so on (the list is garbled in the source).
The text lists the animals dog, cat, monkey, lion, horse, cow and elephant among the wombs of the stars, from Ashvini onward (the source is garbled and the sequence is uncertain).
Enemy pairs: dog and deer, ram and monkey, lion and elephant, cow and tiger, rat and cat, buffalo and horse.
Fish, scorpion and crab are Brahmins; the others above are Kshatriyas and so on. For a man's class-sign with a woman's sign, if lacking, as is auspicious...
For a girl born in the quarters of four, three or two (stars), in order from Ashvini; from Krittika and from the Moon's star...
he should count the nadis by number of three, four, five junctions; death occurs in the same nadi, not in the sides. Prajapatya, Brahma, Daiva marriages and the Arsha join (in)...
at the stated time the four give fruit; the Gandharva, Asura, Paishacha and Rakshasa are always (condemned).
The fourth Abhijit ascendant and the seventh rising star, and the cow-dust time — both give sons and grandsons in marriage.
In the east cow-dust is not the chief for the Kalingas; Abhijit in all countries is the chief, destroying faults.
When the Sun is at midday, the muhurta called Abhijit destroys all faults, as Pinaka-bearer (Shiva) destroyed Tripura.
After a son's marriage, a daughter's marriage should not be in three seasons; nor the thread ceremony of the two after a marriage; in an auspicious rite no other auspicious rite.
If marriages of those born of one (mother) are within six months, without doubt in three years one of them becomes a widow.
A return marriage should not be made, nor two daughters to one man; nor of two men born of one to two girls born of one.
So never a marriage, nor two tonsures at once. One born by day kills the father; by night, the mother;
at twilight, himself; in Ganda there is no reversal. A son or daughter surely kills the father-in-law if born under Mula;
not one born in its last quarter, nor in the first quarter of Ashlesha. Those born in the last quarter of Jyeshtha kill the elder; a boy kills, not a girl.
A girl born under Mula (or Purvashadha) kills neither mother nor father. A girl born under Vishakha kills the husband's elder brother; one under Anuradha, the younger brother-in-law.
From the day of marriage, on the sixth, eighth, tenth or seventh day, the bride's entry (into the house) brings prosperity.
Leaving aside the birth-star, birth-ascendant and birth-day for two years, even with Venus (combust), the wedding-journey is auspicious.
The installation of all gods in the northern course gives prosperity, when the planets of the gods and ancestors are visible.
In the five months from Magha onward except Chaitra, in bright and dark fortnights, in the eight starting from them, it is auspicious.
On the days of each god, in the tithi of that god; on the second and next two, the fifth and next three in order,
the tenth and the four following, especially on the full moon; under the three Uttara stars, Mrigashira, Hasta, three, Jupiter's star,
with Ashvini, Rohini, Shatabhisha, Anuradha, Dhanishta; on days other than Mars's, when the Sun gives strength to the doer,
with Moon and star strong, in the forenoon, on an auspicious day, at a good ascendant and good division, not at the doer's eighth rising.
All signs joined with or aspected by benefics are best; an ascendant with the fifth and eighth purified and the eighth pure.
Moon, Sun, Mars, Rahu, Ketu and Saturn in the ascendant give death to the doer; others give wealth, grain and happiness.
In the second, malefics are not auspicious; benefics and the Moon give wealth. In the third, all planets give sons, grandsons and happiness.
In the fourth, benefics give happiness, cruel ones give grief. In the fifth, cruel ones give weakness, benefics happiness of sons.
In the sixth, benefics give enemies and malefics destroy enemies; in the seventh, malefics give disease and benefics good results.
All planets in the eighth give death to the doer. In the ninth malefics harm and benefics bring welfare.
In the tenth malefics give pain, benefics and the Moon give fame; all planets in the eleventh give much gain.
Planets in the twelfth cause constant great expense; they kill the doer lacking wealth, and the priest lacking mantras;
lacking marks, prosperity... The enemy is not equal to the installation. If the ascendant is of more virtues and the fault is smaller,
the installation of gods there fulfils the doer's wishes. In short, for building, temples, villages, houses and the like,
one should first test the site by its smell, colour, taste and fragments — smelling of honey, flowers, sour things, flesh.
White, red, green and black in order; the tastes sweet, pungent, bitter and astringent in order, for the classes.
A site sloping toward the north-east, east or north brings great increase to men; sloping in other directions brings constant great loss.
Digging a hole a cubit deep and filling it back: if the earth is in excess, great increase; if less, loss; if equal, equal.
Or in the evening, doing that, he fills it with water; if the water is seen in the morning, increase; if muddy, decay.
Thus the site endowed with marks is well examined. To find the directions, he should draw a level circle in the middle.
Setting a twelve-finger gnomon, he should observe the direction; in a squared site, purified by the six-fold division,
on the path of the line a lovely wall should be made; in the four directions, east and the rest, along the lengths,
eight doors in each direction, in order. The fruits of them, in circumambulation order, are:
loss, poverty, gain of wealth, honour from the king, a great forest; theft, great anger, fear — in Indra's direction (east).
Death, bondage, fear, gain of wealth, increase of wealth, endlessness, fear of disease, weakness — in the south.
Loss of sons, increase of enemies, gain of Lakshmi, wealth coming, good fortune, great misfortune, sorrow and grief — in the west.
Loss of wife, weakness, loss; gain of grain and wealth, increase of wealth, fear for a month, illness — in the Moon's direction (north).
In houses and the like the door's height is twice its breadth; the door should be placed in the west or south of the house.
Within the wall he should make the ground of eighty-one squares; in the middle nine squares is the Brahma-place, which is very condemned.
Thirty-two parts all round near the wall: in the Pishacha part the beginning of a house gives sorrow, grief and fear;
the remaining parts in building give sons, grandsons and wealth. The "heads" (veins) of the site are lines arising from the directions, corners and centre;
where the Brahma-parts and Pishacha-parts meet at the heads, there one should know the vital points (marma) and junctions of the site.
Vital points and junctions are not desired, even in a healthy dwelling. The months Magha, Phalguna, Vaishakha, Shravana, Kartika and (Margashirsha)
are the months for house-building, giving sons, health and wealth. In the parts beginning with "a", in the directions east and so on, in order:
ass, horse, lion, dog, serpent, rat, elephant, hare — this is the womb of the directional groups; the fifth from one's own group is the enemy.
One should put the group to be accomplished in front and the accomplisher behind; in reversal, loss of it; in the middle, a debt; auspicious from wealth.
Beginning with the accomplisher's star up to the accomplished, four-fold, divide by seven; the remainder is then the accomplisher's wealth.
The breadth times the length of the house is called its area; from it wealth, debt, income, star, weekday, divisions are counted in order.
A house with more wealth than debt is for increase; with more debt, not good. Uneven income is for good, even income for poverty.
Loss of wealth at the third star, further loss at the fifth star; loss of self at the seventh star, from the husband's star.
Second-twelfth is for poverty, trine for childlessness, sixth-eighth for death; the others are good house-signs.
Sun and Mars days and divisions bring fear of fire; the other planets' days and divisions give success of all desired aims.
In the months from Nabhasya onward, in threes in order, east and so on: head, left side, and the lord, in a circumambulating way.
The "Vastu-man" (spirit of the site) called Chara moves thus, great-bellied; the house should face in the direction the Vastu-man faces.
A house facing the opposite way gives disease, grief and fear. For strong houses with a front door, this fault does not exist.
At the centre of the house, in a hand-deep hole, he should place a brick with gold dust, grain and moss for deposit.
Half the length of the site is the navel; three finger-breadths above it is the belly; there he should plant the peg (shanku), increasing sons and grandsons.
The belly measure for Brahmins and others is twenty-four, twenty-three, sixteen or twelve finger-breadths, adorned with gold, cloth and the like.
Made from khadira, arjuna, shala, red sandal, palasha, red shana or vishala wood — a yoke-machine of wood.
Dividing the peg into three: the first square, then eight-sided, and the third round, smooth and flawless.
Having thus prepared one with marks, on an auspicious day, on ground marked with a cord of the six-fold purity,
under soft, fixed or swift stars, on a day without Rikta and Amavasya, in an ascendant not of Mars's movable sign, with malefics not in the eighth,
with the eighth pure, in a good ascendant and good division, or aspected or joined by benefics, he should plant the peg,
with auspicious proclamations, instruments, auspicious women, with benefics in the third, centre, trine, and others in the third, eleventh, sixth,
with the Moon in the ascendant's division or the eighth, after worshipping the astrologer. Houses with one, two, three, four halls, seven halls, or ten...
those again are sixfold: each ten and sixfold. Dhruva, Dhanya, Jaya, Nanda, Khara, Kanta, Manorama,
Sumukha, Durmukha, Krura, Shatru, Svarnaprada, Kshaya, Akranda, Vipula, Vijaya — sixteen houses.
Thus one counts houses by their layouts. Place the heavy below and the light above in front;
fill behind with heavy ones; all by the light-heavy rule. In the light place one should make a verandah, circumambulating from the house door;
in the verandahs facing east and others are sixteen kinds of houses. The bathing room is in the east, the kitchen in the south-east,
the bedroom in the south, the armoury in the south-west, in the west the dining room, or in the north-west the granary,
in the north the god-house, in the north-east the milk-house; bed, ... dining, auspicious rooms;
grain, women's enjoyment, treasure and places of pleasure: their order from the north-east makes house-building auspicious.
These should be placed in their own directions: Dhvaja, Dhumra, Simha, Shva, Saurameya, Khara, Gaja, Dhvanksha — these eight, in order, are the east-and-others' lords.
Plaksha, udumbara, mango, neem, vibhitaka, ...
milk-trees, ashvattha, kapittha, agasti, sindhuvala, tintidika are condemned.
In the west and south of the house for a man of bilious nature; house-posts of even number are praised, not odd.
Neither too high nor too low, as desired, the height of the wall; so one should reflect everywhere, of houses on houses and the like.
Eight kinds of house-roofs: Panchala-measure, Videha, Kaurava, Kaujanya, Magadha, Shurasena, Gandhara, Avantika.
The height with a fourth of the width is called thus. The measures of Panchala and Matula increase in turn;
the Videha and others are measures in order. The Panchala measure is common to all; beyond that, the Avanti measure for Brahmins, Gandhara for Kshatriyas,
Kaujanya for Vaishyas, and so on in order from Brahmins. As stated, water drainage for two- and three-storeyed houses;
for camel-and elephant-halls, with flag and gain; in animal-sheds and in halls with flag and gain or elephant...
(The lengths of halls by the sets of flag/gain: door, bed, seat, vessels, flag, lion, bull, banner.)
I shall tell the rule of worship of the Vastu on entering a new house.
He should draw ten lines a hand long east-west and ten north-south; in the house centre, above rice, eighty-one squares.
He should draw forty-five gods as will be told; the thirty-two outside are to be worshipped, and the thirteen inside.
I shall now tell their places and names in order. From the north-east corner, outside, these thirty-two gods:
Kripita-yoni, Parjanya, Jayanta, Indra (Pakashasana), Surya, Shashi, Mriga, Akasha, Vayu, Pusha and Nairriti...
